$comment: Payload-size proving ceilings (GitHub #943). Paired with the client resource
guard in frontend/lib/proof-guard.ts: these are the expected cost limits for
the largest proof jobs the app lets a holder request.
How to read this file:
- Each tier names a circuit the harness runs (scripts/perf/measure-payloads.mjs).
Tiers are ordered small → large by the size of the proving job, not by the
wall clock: kyc_proof is one credential, jurisdiction_proof adds an 8-entry
allowlist, aggregate_proof packs two credentials into a single proof.
- maxWitnessMs / maxProveMs are CEILINGS, not regressions: exceeding one means
an allowed payload now costs more than the guard's expected budget, and the
PR fails. Regression-vs-baseline tracking lives in perf/proving-baselines.json
(the existing #629 gate); this file answers "is this payload size still
affordable at all?".
- Values are deliberately generous because runner CPU varies; they are sized
from the provisional medians in perf/proving-baselines.json with headroom
(single credential ≈ 3 s CPU prove, aggregate ≈ 2x that). Tighten them once
several main runs have established the spread.
- maxProveRssMb is a warn-only memory indicator. Peak RSS comes from GNU time
(/usr/bin/time) and is null on runners without it; it never fails a PR.
- scaling.largeToSmallProveRatio catches cost growing faster than payload: the
aggregate proof is ~2x the work of one credential, so a ratio far above that
means the circuit got structurally more expensive.
- To refresh: run the proving-perf workflow on main (workflow_dispatch),
download proving-payloads-report, and update ceilings intentionally with a
$history entry. Raising a ceiling that exists because of a client limit also
requires updating that limit (and, where it comes from a circuit or the
contract, those too) — see docs/PROOF_RESOURCE_LIMITS.md.

$history.change: Initial ceilings (issue #943). Provisional: sized from the existing #629 medians with headroom, to be tightened after the first measured runs on the fixed runner.
